clue.text: Material males?

parts.note: a buck is a male deer, rabbit or hare, and a ram is a male sheep: two males in a row
a buck is a male deer, rabbit or hare, and a ram is a male sheep: two males in a row

explanation.surface: A question about whether a fabric is somehow masculine.
explanation.walkthrough: The one word 'males' supplies two male animals side by side; the question mark warns that the plural is to be read as a pair of different beasts.
explanation.definitionFit: Buckram is a stiff cotton or linen cloth used in bookbinding and to stiffen garments.

clue.text: Wager about the hazard of serving meat

indicators.note: the word for wager goes round the word for hazard

parts.note: a wager is a bet
a hazard is a risk

explanation.surface: Betting on the danger of food poisoning from a meat dish.
explanation.definitionFit: Brisket is a cut of beef from the breast of the animal.

clue.text: Idle dreams of mediaeval dwellings in Iberia

parts.note: castles were the fortified homes of lords in the Middle Ages
Spain covers most of the Iberian peninsula

explanation.surface: Daydreams about living in Spanish fortresses of the Middle Ages.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names impractical daydreams or schemes with no hope of coming true.

clue.text: The government is to draw the line

definitions.meaning: to mark a straight line on paper with a ...

explanation.surface: The authorities decide where to set a limit.
explanation.definitionFit: Rule means control by a governing power, and also to mark straight lines with a ruler.

clue.text: Security services make a con cession for a refugee

parts.note: MI is Military Intelligence, as in the British security services MI5 and MI6
a grant is a concession or allowance given

explanation.surface: Spies grant a special allowance to someone fleeing danger.
explanation.definitionFit: A migrant is a person moving to another country, often fleeing hardship, like a displaced person.

clue.text: Time to seek a job

parts.note: to seek something, such as advice, is to ask for it

explanation.surface: Someone decides the moment has come to go out looking for work.
explanation.definitionFit: A task is a piece of work assigned to someone, the same as a job.

clue.text: Cricketing venue where Theodore meets Valerie

indicators.note: the short form of one name joins up with the short form of the other

parts.note: Theo is the short form of Theodore
Val is the short form of Valerie

explanation.surface: A couple named Theodore and Valerie have their rendezvous at a cricket ground.
explanation.walkthrough: THE OVAL is a London cricket ground, home of Surrey.
explanation.definitionFit: The Kennington ground hosts Surrey matches and Test cricket.

clue.text: Benefit from taking Japanese wine

definitions.meaning: as in 'for the benefit of', for someone's good

explanation.surface: Someone gains by drinking a Japanese rice drink.
explanation.definitionFit: 'For the sake of' means for the good of, and the same spelling names Japanese rice wine.

clue.text: The woman will get the account for the varnish

parts.note: she will contracts to she'll

explanation.surface: A woman will be billed for a coat of varnish.
explanation.definitionFit: Shellac is a resin from the lac insect, dissolved to make a lacquer or varnish.

clue.text: What the ambitious astronaut aspires to do

definitions.text: What the ambitious astronaut aspires to do

parts.words: What the ambitious astronaut aspires to do
parts.note: an astronaut literally rises above the planet, while an ambitious person hopes to rise in status

explanation.surface: A space traveller's career goal.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to rise in social standing or success, and an astronaut would literally climb above the Earth.

clue.text: Reading Plato in the original is quite beyond yours truly

definitions.text: Reading Plato in the original is quite beyond yours truly

parts.words: Reading Plato in the original is quite beyond yours truly
parts.note: Plato wrote in ancient Greek, so reading him untranslated is literally baffling Greek to the speaker, and the idiom for anything incomprehensible names that very language

explanation.surface: A modest admission that classical philosophy in its original language is too hard for the speaker.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom says something is wholly unintelligible to me, and 'yours truly' is a jocular way of saying 'me'.

clue.text: The king takes beer and cabbage

parts.note: K is the chess and card abbreviation for king
ale is a kind of beer

explanation.surface: A monarch's simple meal of beer and greens.
explanation.definitionFit: Kale is a hardy variety of cabbage with curly leaves that do not form a head.

clue.text: Cut right into the middle of the grotto

indicators.note: the word for right is to be pushed into the centre of the word for grotto

parts.note: a grotto is a small cave

explanation.surface: Someone is told to cut a path to the right, deep into the grotto.
explanation.definitionFit: To carve is to cut, as with a joint of meat or a figure in stone.

clue.text: Appeal to father to get a large stone

parts.note: O is the exclamation of address or appeal, as in 'O Lord'
pa is an informal word for father
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A child begs Dad for a big gemstone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Appeal to father' looks like one idea, but 'Appeal' gives the vocative O and 'father' gives PA.
explanation.definitionFit: An opal is a precious gemstone, and 'stone' is the jeweller's everyday word for a gem.

clue.text: Do form a political organisation

definitions.meaning: a do is a social gathering or celebration
a group such as Labour or the Republicans that contests elections

explanation.surface: An instruction to set up a new political group.
explanation.definitionFit: A do is a festive gathering, and a political group contesting elections shares the word.

clue.text: Refuse to fight

definitions.meaning: a noun here: rubbish, waste matter

explanation.surface: Someone declines to get into a brawl.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrap means leftover waste, and also a scuffle or brawl.

clue.text: Rehearsal of play which discriminated against Catholics

parts.note: a rehearsal is a trial run, a test of the performance
an act is a part of a play, or to play a part is to act

explanation.surface: A rehearsal for a drama that touched on religious prejudice.
explanation.walkthrough: The Test Act was English law (1673) requiring public office-holders to take Anglican communion, which shut Catholics out.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1673 statute barred anyone refusing Anglican rites from public office, so it excluded Roman Catholics.

clue.text: Brief study in secular accommodation

indicators.note: the word for study sits inside the word for secular, held there as in lodgings

parts.note: laic means lay or secular, not clerical
to con is an old word meaning to study or learn by heart

explanation.surface: A short spell of study done in non-religious lodgings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accommodation' completes the picture of one piece housed in another, backing up 'in'.
explanation.definitionFit: Laconic speech uses very few words, so it is terse and short.

clue.text: The infant with very little spirit

parts.note: tiny means very small
a tot is a small measure of spirits such as rum

explanation.surface: A baby given only a dash of courage or of drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiny tot is a familiar phrase for a very young child or toddler.

clue.text: A priest is made to do the rounds on foot

indicators.note: the letters are forced into a new form, made into something else

explanation.surface: A clergyman is compelled to walk his parish.
explanation.walkthrough: The seven letters of A PRIEST are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To traipse is to walk wearily from place to place, trudging about.

clue.text: Everyone enters an examination to be top

indicators.note: the word for everyone goes into the word for examination

parts.note: a test is an examination
all means everyone

explanation.surface: All the students sit an exam hoping to come first.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition 'top' is a verb-like 'to be top' reading, but here it is an adjective: highest.
explanation.definitionFit: Tallest means highest of all, standing at the top.

clue.text: Applaud a poor player in Len don

parts.note: to applaud is to clap
a ham is an overacting, poor actor

explanation.surface: Theatre-goers applaud a weak actor on a London stage.
explanation.walkthrough: CLAPHAM is a district of south London, known for Clapham Common and Clapham Junction station.
explanation.definitionFit: The place is a district in south-west London, so it is found within the capital.

clue.text: Fellow revolutionary is given protection

parts.note: cove is old British slang for a fellow or chap
a red is a communist revolutionary

explanation.surface: A comrade in the revolution is granted safe haven.
explanation.definitionFit: Being covered means being shielded or insured against harm.

clue.text: The Scotsman looked wealthy

parts.note: mon is the Scots form of man
eyed means looked at

explanation.surface: A Scotsman seemed prosperous.
explanation.definitionFit: Moneyed means having plenty of money, rich.

clue.text: A record's range

parts.note: an LP is a long-playing record, and the 's adds an S

explanation.surface: Someone asks how wide a span a particular record covers.
explanation.definitionFit: The European mountain chain is a range of peaks.

clue.text: Many are very partial to some garlic

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, which crosswords read as many
to be very partial to something is to love it

explanation.surface: A great many people are fond of a bit of garlic.
explanation.definitionFit: A clove is one segment of a garlic bulb, so a portion of garlic.

clue.text: The bird was set loose before noon

indicators.note: the anagram comes ahead of the letter for noon
the letters of the word are freed from their order and rearranged

explanation.surface: A captive bird was released a little before midday.
explanation.definitionFit: A swan is a large long-necked water bird.

clue.text: Plucky poachers may profit by it

definitions.meaning: wild animals hunted for food or sport, which poachers take illegally

explanation.surface: Bold poachers might make money from what they take.
explanation.definitionFit: Game means brave and willing, and it also names wild animals and birds hunted for sport.

clue.text: Hits back in the boxing-match

indicators.note: the word for hits is read in the backward direction

parts.note: raps are sharp blows or hits

explanation.surface: A boxer strikes back during a bout.
explanation.definitionFit: A spar is a practice bout in boxing.

clue.text: Tommy's estate belongs only to him

definitions.text: Tommy's estate belongs only to him

parts.words: Tommy's estate belongs only to him
parts.note: a Tommy is a British private soldier, so a Tommy's belongings are a private's goods, and land that is one owner's alone takes the same phrase

explanation.surface: A soldier's possessions are his and his alone.
explanation.walkthrough: Tommy (Tommy Atkins) is the nickname for a British private soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: Land or goods owned by an individual rather than the public is described by this phrase, with 'private' doubling for a soldier's rank.

clue.text: In France I get stumped by a joke

parts.note: je is French for I
ST is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for stumped

explanation.surface: A traveller in France finds a joke baffling.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a batsman is out 'stumped' when the wicketkeeper breaks the wicket while he is out of his ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A jest is a joke or witty remark.

clue.text: Free in deed, but treated with contempt

indicators.note: the word for free goes inside the word deed

parts.note: taken as written
to rid is to free, as in rid of a burden

explanation.surface: Someone freed in deed rather than word was nonetheless scorned.
explanation.definitionFit: To be derided is to be mocked or scorned, ridiculed with contempt.
